title: Basis of the Prepay Booking Ceiling on the Crop Input Purchasing Accounts
content:
A prepay booking taken against a signed request the member has lodged is taken at the ceiling the programme will carry where the member has asked for more than that, and the member books it in their own name. The ceiling is worked out on the account's own record, over a window of the 14 statement months before the handling date.

**Prior season spend.** The prior season spend the ceiling is measured on is everything invoiced to the account over the fourteen statement months before the handling date, less every discount granted on the account as a discount line of its own, which is an early pay, volume, prepay or programme rebate discount and never the restocking charge withheld inside a credit memo, rounded half away from zero to two decimal places.

**Ceiling share.** The ceiling share is the share of the prior season spend the programme will carry as prepay.

**Reduction for arrears.** The reduction taken off the ceiling share for arrears on the account is nil.

**Gross ceiling.** The gross ceiling is the prior season spend multiplied by the ceiling share less the reduction taken off it, that difference being taken as nil where it would fall below nil, and the product rounded half away from zero to two decimal places.

**Prepay already standing.** The prepay already standing to the member's credit on the account is the money taken in on prepay bookings less the money since drawn against deliveries, rounded half away from zero to two decimal places. The share of that prepay counted against the gross ceiling is nil.

**The booking taken.** The booking taken is the gross ceiling less the share counted against it of the prepay already standing to the member's credit, that share being rounded half away from zero to two decimal places before it is taken off, and where the remainder falls under the programme's minimum booking the minimum booking is taken instead; the result is rounded half away from zero to two decimal places once at the end.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

A member on a programme of the Crop Input Purchasing Accounts whose ceiling share is 100 percent and whose minimum booking is 10000.00 USD asks for a booking of 300000.00 USD.

| Step | Figure |
| --- | --- |
| Invoiced to the account over the 14 statement months | 240000.00 USD |
| Discount lines granted on the account | 3000.00 USD |
| Prior season spend | 237000.00 USD |
| Ceiling share | 100 percent |
| Reduction taken off the ceiling share | nil |
| Ceiling share less the reduction | 100 percent |
| Gross ceiling | 237000.00 USD |
| Prepay standing to the member's credit | 12000.00 USD |
| Share of it counted against the gross ceiling | nil |
| Money counted against the gross ceiling | 0.00 USD |
| Booking taken | 237000.00 USD |

The member asked for more than the ceiling, so the booking is taken at 237000.00 USD. Had the remainder come out under the programme's minimum booking of 10000.00 USD, the booking taken would have been 10000.00 USD.
